newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Sulzer unit cuts jobs, takes charge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sulzer unit cuts jobs, takes charge.

text.p: Swiss weaving machine maker Sulzer Rueti on Thursday said it would cut nearly a third of 3,200 jobs and take a charge of up to 36 million Swiss francs ($28.39 million) that will lower 1996 group profits at parent Sulzer AG.

Sulzer Rueti, which has lost money in four of the past five years, said it aimed to regain profitibility despite a shrinking world market by slashing jobs and concentrating production at one rather than two Swiss plants.
Sulzer Rueti division president Helmut Pirchl said 950 jobs would be cut through end-1997, most through redundancies, in a programe costing "several dozen millions" of Swiss francs.
"The group net profit will be worsened correspondingly," Pirchl told a news conference.
Pirchl declined to specify the amount more closely. "A large amount (of the costs) will be taken in provisions this year," he added.
But a Sulzer official who declined to be named said 1996 provisions for cut-backs at Sulzer Rueti should not exceed about 36 million Swiss francs.
"It shouldn't be more than three dozen million in 1996 provisions (for the job cuts)," the executive told Reuters.

It was the second blow to 1996 profit prospects in one month at Sulzer AG, an engineering group with five core areas from pumping equipment to medical technology whose net profit plunged by over half from 1994 to 92 million Swiss francs.

Sulzer last cut its profit forecast on September 26, saying it expected a lower result than in 1995 due to about 45 million Swiss francs needed to pay damages in a U.S. patent case against Sulzer unit Intermedica Orthopedics.

Sulzer shares were slightly higher at around 762 Swiss francs in late trade following the news after closing at 760 on Thursday following several days of advances in anticipation of the Sulzer Rueti announcement.

Sulzer Rueti is the world's leading manufacturer of shuttleless weaving machines and is hard hit by a steady decline in demand since 1990, as the productivity of weaving amchines has risen and world textile demand has stalled.

Pirchl said Sulzer Rueti's loss this year would be at least double the 1995 deficit of 34 million Swiss francs, with machinery orders down 30 percent in the first nine months compared to the same period last year.

By ending production at its smaller plant in the town of Rueti near Zurich and concentrating on a second Swiss plant in Zuchwil, Pirchl said Sulzer Rueti could reduce its production capacity to less than half of the 1990 level by the end of 1997.
"That is in line with the world market, which will be half the 1990 size in 1996," Pirchl said.
Sulzer Rueti said in a statement 600 job cuts were planned in Rueti, 300 in Zuchwil and 50 in the 210-strong non-production workforce outside Switzerland.
